scope: P5 fit: pair-diff delivery axis vs the banked oracle axis. A zero-token decision: no model loaded, no token generated, no merge spent.
command: uv run python scripts/pair_axis_check.py --records verification/q3-4b-frames/frames.pt --verdicts verification/q3-4b-frames/pairs.jsonl --oracle verification/q3-4b-oracle-control/q3oaxes135 --out verification/p5/pair-axis-check.json

gate_run.records: verification/q3-4b-frames/frames.pt (32,181,889 bytes; *.pt is gitignored, on disk beside its committed capture report; sha256 b7b0c033e23d95e4...)
gate_run.verdicts: verification/q3-4b-frames/pairs.jsonl (1 candidate, verdict other, reader hermes#2372)
gate_run.reading: 0 vetted delivery pairs < 10, so no axis was fitted, no cos was computed, and no merge is justified. This is the card's gate 3, not a cos result.

decision_is_blocked_not_negative: There is no mean cos for the real pair axis. The dependency card (t_40519564) banked one shape-delivery candidate and the agent read rejected it ('other'), so the fit the card asks for has no data. Do not read 'insufficient' as 'orthogonal'.

oracle_axes_missing.consequence: with >= 10 vetted pairs the command exits 2: 'oracle directory verification/q3-4b-oracle-control/q3oaxes135 holds no .pt axes file'; the script accepts the .pt path directly or --oracle-key when a file is restored
oracle_axes_missing.recovery: scripts/recover_oracle_axes.py <out.pt> <base.gguf> <oracle.gguf> writes {axes_attn, axes_ffn}; neither the q3-4b base q8 nor the published heretic gguf is on this host, so recovery here would need a multi-GB download
oracle_axes_missing.verified: the exit-2 message was printed on a 10-pair fixture pointed at that directory

identical_axis.prints: table + 'decision: DEAD - ... rank-1 delivery hypothesis dead (expect the same read)'

orthogonal_axis.prints: table + 'decision: ORTHOGONAL - ... orthogonal, one merge test justified'

deliver_without_verdict.prints: deliver record without a verdict: row-unread[frame=seed]

fixture_checks.tests: tests/test_pair_axis_check.py (7 cases) asserts both fixture outcomes from stdout, not from the packet

thresholds.between: inconclusive - report only, do not spend a merge

sign_convention: the decision uses |cos| because an axis and its negation are the same merge target; signed mean and min are reported in the packet beside it
not_a_claim: No delivery, merge or capability claim. The packet records counts and, on a sufficient corpus, a cos number only.
